title: Gluten-Free Chocolate Chip Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft gluten-free vanilla cupcakes loaded with mini chocolate chips, ready in about 43 minutes total with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a classic chocolate chip cookie in cake form. I tested this batter three times in my own kitchen to get a gluten-free crumb that stays soft, not gritty. The trick is tossing the mini chips in almond flour before folding them in. That light coating keeps every chip suspended in the batter instead of sinking to the bottom. A gluten-free flour blend with xanthan gum gives the crumb structure, and buttermilk keeps it moist. The vanilla buttercream on top is simple and lets the chocolate chips stay the star. This is a good pick for birthday parties where you need one gluten-free tray that still tastes like a normal cupcake.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups gluten-free all-purpose flour blend (with xanthan gum)
3/4 cup mini chocolate chips, plus 2 tbsp for topping
1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the gluten-free flour blend, 6 tablespoons almond flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In a small bowl, toss the mini chocolate chips with the remaining 2 tablespoons almond flour to coat them.
Beat the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla extract.
Add the dry mix in two batches, alternating with the buttermilk. Mix just until combined.
Fold in the coated chocolate chips by hand so they stay evenly spread through the batter.
Divide batter among liners, filling each about two thirds full. Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the frosting, beat the butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar, cream, vanilla, and salt. Beat 3 minutes until fluffy.
Pipe or spread frosting on the cooled cupcakes and finish with the reserved mini chocolate chips.
tips: Coating the mini chips in almond flour is the real fix for sinking. Do not skip this step.
Use room temperature eggs and butter so the batter mixes smoothly without curdling.
Do not overbake. Gluten-free crumb dries out fast, so pull the pan at 16 minutes and check.
If your gluten-free blend has no xanthan gum, add 1/4 teaspoon to the dry mix.

faq.question: Why do chocolate chips sink in gluten-free cupcakes?
faq.answer: Gluten-free batter is often thinner than wheat batter, so heavy mini chips drop before the cupcake sets. Tossing the chips in almond flour adds light coating and friction that keeps them suspended.

faq.question: Can I use regular chocolate chips instead of mini chips?
faq.answer: Mini chips work better here because they spread evenly and stay lighter in the batter. Regular chips are heavier and more likely to sink even with the almond flour trick.

faq.question: What gluten-free flour blend works best for this recipe?
faq.answer: Use a 1 to 1 gluten-free blend that already includes xanthan gum, like Bob's Red Mill or King Arthur Measure for Measure. This keeps the crumb from turning gummy or crumbly.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy free?
faq.answer: Swap the butter for a plant based butter stick and use unsweetened almond milk with 1 teaspoon vinegar instead of buttermilk. The texture stays close to the original.

conclusion: These gluten-free chocolate chip cupcakes prove you do not need wheat flour for a soft, bakery style crumb. Toss those mini chips in almond flour and they will stay put through every bite.
